text: Every part depends on one number: the temperature of the mould steel.
Here's what holds it.
The mould temperature controller.
It's a pump, a heater and a cooling valve in one box, connected to the mould by hoses.
The pump drives water out to the mould and through its channels,
picking up heat from the hot plastic, then back to the unit.
A sensor measures the water temperature.
Too cold? The heater switches on.
Too hot? The cooling valve opens, and water from the tower carries the heat away.
The controller balances the two, to hold the setpoint within a degree.
But the water is the problem.
Hard water leaves scale on the heater, so it runs hotter and burns out.
Dirt jams the cooling valve. Stuck shut, the mould overheats. Stuck open, it can't hold temperature.
Pump seals wear and leak, and hoses crack from the heat.
Warning signs: temperature that swings or overshoots, slow heat-up, pressure alarms, and water under the unit.
So: use treated water, and descale the unit and the mould circuits on a schedule.
Clean the strainer, and check the cooling valve opens and closes.
Inspect the hoses, and test the over-temperature cut-out.
Always cool down and depressurise before opening it. Hot water under pressure burns.
Steady steel. Steady parts.
